Select the initial two-carburettor 105 CV version, not the later 115 CV development or three-carburettor 127 CV tune. cars.summary: The 8V marked Fiat’s return to purpose-built sporting GTs with its distinctive V8, independent suspension at both ends and aerodynamic Rapi body. Its documented privateer competition success, including a two-litre class victory at Monza in 1954, supports a lasting performance identity beyond rarity.

cars.specification_market: Selected 58 HP collection entry dated 1972 in the manufacturer’s 12 April 2024 retrospective; introduction was in September 1971. Later 1050-cc/70 HP engines and gearbox developments are excluded. The downloaded 1983 manual is not evidence for this early specification. One family is counted, including Lancia-badged export aliases. The representative later-series photograph does not establish the selected engine or year.
cars.summary: The A112 Abarth brought Carlo Abarth’s sporting approach to an accessible small road car. Its place in the Fiat Group’s driver-development trophy makes this an enduring compact performance family rather than an ordinary A112.

cars.specification_market: Audi Tradition’s 27 October 2023 history separates standard TTS road cars from track-only Speed Set equipment. Preserve its rounded one-litre displacement rather than infer an exact capacity. No ordinary Prinz output, TT tune, Jägermeister racing engine, race speed or competition carburettors are transferred. One TT/TTS family is counted; 1967 is programme context, not the pictured museum car’s certified year.
cars.summary: The TT/TTS family made the lightweight rear-engined NSU an enduring club-motorsport icon. Its long hill-climbing success and factory sporting chassis distinguish it from the ordinary Prinz, while the selected standard TTS remains a road car.
